messages:
sanjay: Heads-up — planning a rolling cordon + reboot of the az-west1 GPU cohort tonight 00:30–03:30 UTC. Purpose: NIC microcode + driver bump and kernel hotpatch. Expect short connection resets and small tail-latency spikes for ~2–4% of requests. We'll drain workloads gracefully and backfill where possible.
anya: Sounds good. How big are cohorts? can we keep per-cohort impact <5%?
sanjay: We're doing 12–15 node cohorts (based on current pool sizes) staggered every 10m. That yields ~6 cohorts. Canary in saturn-canary first (3 nodes).
rui: I'll disable any aggressive scale-to-zero policies for the window so warmups don't thrash. Also will set autoscaler max surge to +10% to allow short backfill.
maya: Please pre-seed prefix/KV cache on canary after reboot. Cold cache is the main source of tail tokens. Run kv-warm on canary and then parallel to cohorts.
liam: If we need immediate capacity spike we'll spin cloud-burst GPUs — estimate cost for the window ~ $4.2k (on-demand). Cheaper to reserve dedicated for steady need but not worth it for a 3h window.
anya: Can we try soft-drain first (no forced evict) so in-flight jobs finish? Some batch tenants have long runs.
sanjay: Yes — soft drain then wait 5m for graceful termination, then force drain if pods still present. Command:
```
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force --grace-period=300
```
maya: After reboot, run KV warm: `./tools/kv-warm --pool saturn --parallel 8 --prefixes-file prefixes.txt` — will reduce token churn.
liam: Ops question — will routing send traffic to other regions? Any egress cost or latency impact for customers pinned to az-west1?
sanjay: Routing policy: latency-first for paid tiers, region-fallback for others. We'll notify routing to prefer eu-west1 for pinned workloads only as a last resort. Expected extra egress ~100GB, estimate ~$30 for the window.
ops-bot: maintenance created: MNT-2026-0427 (az-west1 NIC/driver) scheduled 2026-04-27 00:30–03:30 UTC. PagerDuty notified.
oncall-bot: @oncall rotation alerted: sanjay and rui assigned primary during maintenance.
rui: I'll watch scheduler pressure and eviction rates. If eviction > 1% for >10m we abort cohort and roll back.
anya: What about long-running interactive sessions? We should pin a small spare pool for them and route there.
sanjay: Agreed — reserving 6 nodes in `interactive-spare` for session continuity. If we need burst beyond that, liam will approve cloud-burst.
maya: Reminder: after first cohort, run perf smoke: `./scripts/gpu-smoke --seq-len 512 --qps 50 --duration 60s` and post graphs to #eng-metrics.
liam: I'll publish cost rundown post-window. Quick calc: burst GPUs + egress + small ops tools ~= $4.5k worst-case. Approve? :money_with_wings:
sanjay: Approved for this window. Keep tight telemetry.
anya: I'll draft customer comms for impacted tenants (low-traffic note + link to status page).
maya: tagging owners for model rollouts that might be sensitive to kernel change: @mlops please double-check evals tomorrow morning.
liam: ack :thumbsup:
sanjay: Final checklist: 1) canary at 00:30 2) preseed cache 3) run smoke perf 4) step cohorts every 10m 5) abort criteria ready. If no major regressions we continue.
ops-bot: Postmortem template queued on completion.
rui: I'll keep this channel open during the window. Ping me if you see p95 > baseline + 25%.
anya: ok, team — see you on the ops call 00:15 UTC for preflight. :coffee:
